patterns.note: Asymmetrical two-column layout for content sections, often with a large image on one side and text on the other, connected by a strong vertical timeline element.
Very large, bold, sans-serif headings are used for key section titles, creating strong visual hierarchy against smaller, lighter body text.
High-contrast black and white scheme is dominant, with a deep dark blue/grey for overlays and subtle text, and a vibrant yellow used sparingly for interactive elements and calls to action.
A sticky navigation bar at the top of the page transforms on scroll, shrinking slightly and gaining a solid background.
Content sections, particularly the timeline elements, reveal themselves with a subtle fade-in or slide-up effect as they enter the viewport.
A distinctive black footer features a large, abstract, dotted representation of the company logo (PXP) as a prominent graphic element.

technique_notes: A full-bleed hero section uses a background video with a dark, semi-transparent overlay to ensure text readability.
The primary navigation bar is implemented as a sticky element that changes its height and background color after a certain scroll threshold.

Scroll-triggered animations (likely using CSS keyframes as hinted) are used to progressively reveal content sections, such as the timeline entries, with a subtle upward slide and fade effect as they become visible.

design_tokens.type_scale: Very large, bold sans-serif headings (~3-4x body text) create strong visual impact, contrasted with smaller, lighter body text and uppercase navigation.
design_tokens.spacing: balanced to airy, with generous vertical spacing between major sections and within the timeline structure, creating a sense of openness

standout: The most distinctive feature is the highly graphic, almost brutalist use of a vertical timeline to structure the main content, combined with the bold, dotted PXP logo in the footer. This creates a unique blend of corporate professionalism and artistic expression.
